title: Session 1: RDBMS Concepts - Quiz — Intelligent Data Management with SQL Server

questions.questionText: A database is best described as:
options: An organized collection of related data
questions.correctAnswer: An organized collection of related data
questions.explanation: A database is an organized form of data, consisting of related data items to which different questions can be asked.

questions.questionText: The session gives examples like 'What are the phone numbers and addresses of the five nearest post offices?' to illustrate that a database can be thought of as:
options: A data collection to which different questions can be asked
questions.correctAnswer: A data collection to which different questions can be asked
questions.explanation: The session frames a database as a data collection that can answer various questions posed against it.

questions.questionText: According to the session, data becomes information when it is:
questions.explanation: When data is gathered and analyzed, it yields information, which helps foresee and plan events.

questions.questionText: Data management deals with managing large amounts of information through which two approaches described in the session?
questions.explanation: The session describes file-based systems and database systems as the two approaches to data management.

questions.questionText: In file-based systems, files of archived data were called 'tables' because they resembled:
options: Tables used in traditional file keeping
questions.correctAnswer: Tables used in traditional file keeping
questions.explanation: Files of archived data were called tables because they looked like tables used in traditional file keeping.

questions.questionText: In a file-based system, rows in a table were traditionally called:
questions.explanation: Rows in the table were called records, and columns were called fields, in traditional file-based systems.

questions.questionText: In a file-based system, columns were traditionally called:
questions.explanation: Columns in a file-based system's table were called fields.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is NOT listed as a disadvantage of file-based systems?
questions.explanation: Centralized security control is actually an advantage of database systems, not a disadvantage of file-based systems.

questions.questionText: When the same customer data is duplicated across two files and a change to one is not reflected in the other, this illustrates:
questions.explanation: Storing the same data in multiple private files causes redundancy, and inconsistency arises if a change in one file isn't reflected in the other.

questions.questionText: Difficulty handling a sudden request such as listing all customers with an account balance of $20,000 or more illustrates the file-based system issue of:
questions.explanation: Unplanned/ad-hoc queries are difficult to handle in file-based systems since a program to generate the required list may not exist.

questions.questionText: When related data is scattered across isolated files that may be in different formats, this is called:
questions.explanation: Data isolation refers to related data being scattered across isolated files, possibly in different formats.

questions.questionText: Difficulty in allowing multiple users to access the same file or record simultaneously in a file-based system is known as:
questions.explanation: In large multi-user systems, handling simultaneous access to the same file or record is difficult in a file-based system — a concurrent access anomaly.

questions.questionText: Restricting payroll staff so they cannot view customer account data illustrates the file-based system issue of:
questions.explanation: This is a security problem — enforcing that users only access the data relevant to them is difficult in ad-hoc file-based applications.

questions.questionText: The rule 'Customer ID, which is the unique identifier for a customer record, should not be empty' is an example of:
questions.explanation: This is a data integrity rule — a condition/constraint that must be maintained on data elements.

questions.questionText: According to the session, database systems evolved in which period to address common issues in file-based applications?
questions.explanation: Database Systems evolved in the late 1960s to address common issues found in file-based systems.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is an advantage of database systems mentioned in the session?
questions.explanation: A centralized database system reduces redundancy by helping the same data be accessed by many departments instead of duplicated.

questions.questionText: Updating a single centralized record when Mr. Larry Finner is promoted, instead of updating multiple files, illustrates:
questions.explanation: Because there is just one record to change in a central database, data inconsistency is reduced.

questions.questionText: In a centralized database system, who is typically given full control to modify the database and implement security restrictions?
questions.explanation: The person with full control over the database, called the Database Administrator (DBA), implements security by placing restrictions on data.

questions.questionText: A DBMS (Database Management System) can be defined as:
options: A collection of related records and a set of programs to access and manipulate them
questions.correctAnswer: A collection of related records and a set of programs to access and manipulate them
questions.explanation: A DBMS is defined as a collection of related records and a set of programs that access and manipulate these records.

questions.questionText: Defining the structure of data — including field types, sizes, and constraints — is part of a DBMS's:
questions.explanation: Data definition provides functions to define the structure of data, including record structure, field types/sizes, and constraints.

questions.questionText: Inserting, modifying, or deleting data — handling both planned and unplanned requirements — falls under a DBMS's:
questions.explanation: Data manipulation covers inserting, modifying, or deleting data, handling both planned and unplanned (ad-hoc) requirements.

questions.questionText: Queries that are performed as and when required, without being pre-planned as part of an application, are called:
questions.explanation: Unplanned queries are ad-hoc queries performed as and when required.

questions.questionText: The DBMS component that evaluates different implementations of a query and chooses the best one is the:
questions.explanation: A DBMS has a Query Optimizer, a set of programs that evaluates different implementations of a query and picks the best one, for performance.

questions.questionText: SQL (Structured Query Language) is best described in the session as a:
questions.explanation: SQL is a non-procedural query language, where the user requests what is required without specifying how it is to be done.

questions.questionText: Which of these are cited as examples of procedural languages that can also provide data access to programmers?
options: None — only SQL provides data access
questions.explanation: The session lists C, Visual Basic, and Pascal as procedural languages that also provide data access to programmers.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is NOT listed in the session as an example of a database application?
questions.explanation: The examples listed are computerized library systems, automated teller machines, flight reservation systems, and computerized parts inventory systems — not word processing software.

questions.questionText: Sophisticated languages used for managing database systems are referred to as:
questions.explanation: Sophisticated languages for managing database systems are called Fourth Generation Languages (4GLs).

questions.questionText: In the Flat File Data Model, the database consists of:
questions.explanation: The Flat File Data Model uses only one table or file and is suited to simple databases, but can cause redundancy.

questions.questionText: Which database model represents data using a tree-like structure in which a child record can have only one parent?
questions.explanation: In the Hierarchical Model, relationships are structured as children and parents, and a child can have only one parent.

questions.questionText: Which real-world system is cited in the session as an example of the Hierarchical Data Model?
questions.explanation: The Windows Registry is given as an example of a hierarchical database storing configuration settings and options.

questions.questionText: In the Hierarchical Model example (Department, Project, Employee), which segments are the children of the DEPARTMENT segment?
questions.explanation: In the figure, Department is the parent segment, and Project and Employee are its children.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is an advantage of the Hierarchical model mentioned in the session?
options: Data independence provided by a DBMS reduces effort and cost in maintaining the program
It requires no DBMS at all
It cannot handle large volumes of data
Only a single user can ever access the data
questions.correctAnswer: Data independence provided by a DBMS reduces effort and cost in maintaining the program
questions.explanation: Advantages listed include easier data sharing/security via a DBMS, and data independence which reduces effort and costs in maintaining the program.

questions.questionText: The Network Data Model differs from the Hierarchical Model mainly because:
options: It does not use tables at all
A child record is allowed to have more than one parent
It cannot store large amounts of data
It uses only a single file
questions.correctAnswer: A child record is allowed to have more than one parent
questions.explanation: Unlike the hierarchical model's single-parent tree, the network model uses set theory allowing a child to have more than one parent.

questions.questionText: Which organization defined the structures and language constructs of the network model?
questions.explanation: The network model structures and language constructs were defined by CODASYL.

questions.questionText: Which of these are given as examples of a Network DBMS in the session?
questions.explanation: IDMS (from Computer Associates) and Raima Database Manager (from Raima Inc.) are given as examples of Network DBMS.

questions.questionText: In network model terminology, the definition of a database's name, record types, and the components making up records is called its:
questions.explanation: This overall definition for a database is called its network schema.

questions.questionText: The portion of a network database as seen by the application's programs is referred to as the:
questions.explanation: The sub-schema is the portion of the database seen by application programs, allowing them to access required data.

questions.questionText: In the Relational Model, a row is referred to as a:
questions.explanation: In relational model terminology, a row is called a tuple.

questions.questionText: In the Relational Model, a column is referred to as an:
questions.explanation: In relational model terminology, a column is called an attribute, and the table itself is called a relation.

questions.questionText: The number of tuples in a relation determines its:
questions.explanation: Cardinality of a relation is determined by the number of tuples (rows) it contains.

questions.questionText: The number of attributes in a relation determines its:
questions.explanation: The degree of a relation is the number of attributes (columns) it has.

questions.questionText: The set of all values that a particular attribute can take is called its:
questions.explanation: The domain of an attribute is the list/set of values applicable to that particular field.

questions.questionText: Which of these is NOT mentioned in the session as a popular relational DBMS?
questions.explanation: Oracle, Sybase, DB2, and Microsoft SQL Server are named as popular relational DBMSs; the Windows Registry is a hierarchical database example, not relational.

questions.questionText: An attribute or combination of attributes that uniquely identifies each tuple in a relation is called the:
questions.explanation: The Primary Key of a relation is an attribute or combination of attributes that uniquely defines each tuple.

questions.questionText: An attribute in one relation whose values must match those in another relation, indicating a relationship between the two, is called a:
questions.explanation: A Foreign Key in relation R1 indicates a relationship with relation R2, and must contain values matching those in R2.

questions.questionText: In the Order_August / Customer example from the session, which column acts as a foreign key referencing the Customer table?
questions.explanation: Cust_No in the Order_August relation is a foreign key creating a reference to the Customer relation.

questions.questionText: An advantage of the relational model mentioned in the session is that it:
options: Is always faster than every other database model
Lets programmers concentrate on the logical view of the database rather than the physical view
Requires no query language at all
questions.correctAnswer: Lets programmers concentrate on the logical view of the database rather than the physical view
questions.explanation: A key advantage is that the relational model lets programmers focus on the logical view rather than being bothered with the physical view.

questions.questionText: A disadvantage of the relational model noted in the session is that it:
options: Cannot store large volumes of data
Tends to be slower than other database systems despite hiding system complexities
Has no concept of primary keys
Is rarely used compared to other models
questions.correctAnswer: Tends to be slower than other database systems despite hiding system complexities
questions.explanation: Though it hides system complexities, the relational model tends to be slower than other database models.

questions.questionText: A Relational Database Management System (RDBMS) is best defined as:
options: A software program that helps create, maintain, and manipulate a relational database
questions.correctAnswer: A software program that helps create, maintain, and manipulate a relational database
questions.explanation: An RDBMS is a software program that helps create, maintain, and manipulate a relational database.

questions.questionText: In a relational database, tables are related to one another mainly through:
questions.explanation: By having common keys, or fields, among tables, data from multiple tables can be joined to form one large resultset.

questions.questionText: According to the session, a key difference between a DBMS and an RDBMS is that:
options: A DBMS is always more secure than an RDBMS
An RDBMS enforces tabular relationships between data items, while a DBMS does not require this
A DBMS supports client/server architecture while an RDBMS does not
An RDBMS is a single-user system while a DBMS is multi-user
questions.correctAnswer: An RDBMS enforces tabular relationships between data items, while a DBMS does not require this
questions.explanation: An RDBMS requires tabular structure and enforces table relationships, while a DBMS does not require data to be in tabular form.

questions.questionText: An entity, as defined in the session, is:
options: A person, place, thing, object, event, or concept that can be distinctly identified
Only a numeric value stored in a database
questions.correctAnswer: A person, place, thing, object, event, or concept that can be distinctly identified
questions.explanation: An entity is a person, place, thing, object, event, or even a concept that can be distinctly identified — for example, students, faculty, and courses in a university.

questions.questionText: A grouping of related entities, given a name reflecting its contents, is called:
questions.explanation: A grouping of related entities becomes an entity set, such as all students being stored in an entity set called Student.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is NOT one of the characteristics of a table listed in the session?
options: Each column has a distinct name
Each table must have a primary key that uniquely identifies each row
The order of the rows and columns matters in a DBMS
Each row/column intersection represents a single data value
questions.correctAnswer: The order of the rows and columns matters in a DBMS
questions.explanation: The session states the order of the rows and columns is immaterial (does not matter) in a DBMS — the opposite of option C.
